problems.title: PF density sign
problems.check: Continuity equation and independent Gaussian derivative
problems.counterevidence: Active diffusion_utils.py:178-209 uses the correct sign. Appendix D.3 Eq.(20) has a path/density sign inconsistency and is not positive counterevidence.
problems.impact: Wrong printed identity; active importance-sampling failure not established
problems.correction: Replace the leading minus by plus in Eq.(7)

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Independently read physical p.3 Eqs.(3)-(8), p.19 Eq.(20), and the static diffusion_utils.py:178-209 anchors. Smooth positive Gaussian p_t=N(0,1+t^2), sigma=t>0 satisfies the VE convolution and characteristic assumptions.
independent_check.decisive_check: Continuity gives material derivative -div(f), f=-t score, hence +t Hessian(log p_t). Along x=c sqrt(1+t^2), log p=-0.5 log(2 pi (1+t^2))-0.5 c^2, derivative -t/(1+t^2), while the printed Eq.(7) gives +t/(1+t^2). At t=1 the values are -0.5 and +0.5. In code, x_new=x+(x-D)/t * (t_next-t) and log_prob_new=log_prob-div(f)*(t_next-t), so reversing integration does not change the correct continuity sign.
independent_check.counterevidence: The active nonmolecular PF path uses the consistent sign. Fresh inspection of the physical p.19 image shows Eq.(20) is not valid positive counterevidence as previously stated: the displayed path has a minus before integral from 1 to t, hence xdot=-f_tilde, while its density identity uses the sign appropriate to xdot=+f_tilde. The report now records this inconsistency instead of claiming the whole pair is correct.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor retained for the incorrect printed identities; the release supplies counterevidence against attributing this sign to importance weights. Fix Eq.(7) leading sign; for Eq.(20), make path and density signs consistent (changing path minus to plus gives the displayed density integral). This does not validate every density estimator or historical run.

problems.title: W1 returned as W2 in data branch
problems.check: Reference repeated origin; A distances [0,4], B distances [2.1,2.1]
problems.counterevidence: Current commit not authenticated as historical experiment commit; no claim of actual benchmark reversal
problems.impact: Proved release-definition discrepancy; effect on central published comparisons Needs Evidence
problems.correction: Optimize squared distances then take square root; no revised benchmark verified

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read Appendix B physical p.14 Eq.(15), metrics.py:93-119 and :215-220, and eval.py Wasserstain2_data call. Inputs are finite 2D tensors with equal empirical weights and Euclidean ground metric.
independent_check.decisive_check: For empirical reference at the origin twice, every admissible coupling has the same row-weighted costs. Candidate radii (0,4) have linear cost 2 and squared-cost root sqrt(8); constant radii (2.1,2.1) give both 2.1. Therefore the observed optimize-linear-cost branch is W1 and rankings need not agree with Eq.(15). G.sum=1, so its division cannot supply a square or root.
independent_check.counterevidence: The release has separate 1D and SE(3) branches, not covered by this specific proof. Current commit and plotted W2 labels do not establish historical experiment provenance; no actual benchmark reversal follows from the synthetic example.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor release-definition defect with published impact Needs Evidence. Repair squared ground costs before minimization, then square root; an output-only square root is insufficient. This directly concerns the principal sample-space metric but the missing historical implementation prevents asserting core empirical damage.

problems.title: TVD drops out-of-range generated mass
problems.result: Release calculation 0; full empirical TV 0.5; two of four generated values retained
problems.counterevidence: Paper discloses energy-histogram limitations and exclusions; historical magnitude unmeasured
problems.impact: Release metric silently conditional; published impact Needs Evidence
problems.correction: Preserve all sample mass with overflow bins or encompassing range, retaining stated binning scope

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read Eq.(16) and Appendix B full-space/energy-histogram wording; static 1D branch metrics.py:57-70. Four finite reference values [0,0,1,1] and generated [0,1,100,100] satisfy the branch dimensions and are nonempty.
independent_check.decisive_check: The reference-derived [0,1] bin range retains both reference endpoints but only generated 0,1. Separate count normalizations yield equal histograms, TV=0. Full empirical masses on {0,1,100} give half*(1/4+1/4+1/2)=1/2. This is lost mass, distinct from ordinary bin-coarsening bias.
independent_check.counterevidence: Energy histograms cannot identify full state-space distributions, which the report already distinguishes. The 2D implementation uses combined ranges, so this conclusion is limited to the 1D branch. Appendix B exclusion of undefined runs does not recover discarded finite outliers.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor release defect; quantify benchmark influence only with retained samples and historical code. Common encompassing range or overflow bins prevents this loss of probability mass but does not make a binned statistic exact continuous TV.

problems.title: MMD convention mismatch
problems.result: Eq.(17)=2; Eq.(18)=4; release squared statistic convention
problems.counterevidence: MMD squared is legitimate if labeled; fixed-kernel nonnegative ranking preserved
problems.correction: Remove outer square root in Eq.(17); reconcile MMD versus MMD-squared labels

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read physical p.15 Eqs.(17)-(18) and Gaussian-kernel source arithmetic at metrics.py:23-54. The RKHS definition is general; k(x,y)=xy is positive semidefinite and the point masses have finite moments.
independent_check.decisive_check: Unit-ball functions ax with |a|<=1 give sup E_P f-E_Q f=4 for delta0,delta4 (choose a=-1). Eq.(17) gives sqrt(4)=2 while Eq.(18) gives sqrt(16)=4. The code averages XX+YY-XY-YX, so it is a squared estimator regardless of the particular Gaussian kernel used there; the linear example is not claimed to reproduce that code kernel.
independent_check.counterevidence: Squared MMD is a legitimate labeled statistic, and for a common fixed kernel its nonnegative population ranking agrees with MMD. A data-dependent bandwidth changes the common-kernel premise, so no universal cross-run ranking statement is made.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor convention and units mismatch, no demonstrated core sampler failure. Remove the outer root on the supremum and label the release MMD squared or take the appropriate root; no full metric rerun was performed.
